svg.title: Confidence, and the decision to say nothing. score = completeness times (closeness times 0.5 plus separation times 0.5). Completeness: how much of your body you told us. Closeness: how well the winning size fits. Separation: how clearly it beats the runner up. Completeness is a ceiling, not another term to average: 0 measurements 0, 1 measurement 0.55, 2 measurements 0.8, 3 measurements 1. High confidence needs a score of 0.72 or more, so a one measurement profile can reach medium but never high. Medium is 0.45 up to 0.72; below 0.45 no size is named. Sitting exactly between two sizes scores near zero on separation and is withheld however complete the profile is. A sold out size substitution multiplies the score by 0.8. Shoppers see High or Medium, never a percentage, because there is no validation data behind the heuristic.

section.h2: Between two sizes? It says so.

ul.li: completenessHow much of your body you told us. A ceiling, not a term to average in.
closenessHow well the winning size fits those measurements.
separationHow clearly it beats the runner up. A tie is a coin flip, not an answer.
Exactly between two sizes: separation near zero, so no size is named, however complete the profile.
Substituting a sold out size multiplies the score by 0.8.
Shoppers see High or Medium. Never a percentage: there is no validation data behind it.
